en: Puggalapaññatti Matrix 1.
The Singlefold Exposition (Ekakauddesa)
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
There are six designations:
the designation of aggregates, the designation of sense-bases, the designation of elements, the designation of truths, the designation of faculties, and the designation of persons.
To what extent is there a designation of aggregates for the aggregates?
To the extent of the five aggregates:
the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.
To this extent is there the designation of aggregates for the aggregates.
To what extent is there the designation of bases for the bases?
To the extent that there are twelve bases.

The eye-base, the form-base, the ear-base, the sound-base, the nose-base, the odor-base, the tongue-base, the taste-base, the body-base, the tangible-object-base, the mind-base, and the mental-phenomena-base:
to this extent is there a designation of the bases as "bases.
To what extent is there a designation of the elements as "elements"?
To the extent that there are eighteen elements:
the eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element;
the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element;... [and so forth].
The body element, the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, the mind element, the mental-phenomena element, and the mind-consciousness element:
to this extent is there a designation of elements for the elements.
To what extent is there a designation of truths for the truths?
To the extent that there are four truths—
the truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path—
to that extent is there the designation of truths.
To what extent is there a designation of the faculties (*indriya*)?
To the extent that there are twenty-two faculties:
the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty...
The faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity, the life faculty, the faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of mental joy,
the faculty of mental grief, the faculty of equanimity, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom,
the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has known.
To this extent is there a designation of faculties as "faculties.
To what extent is there a designation of persons as "persons"?
One liberated by occasion.
One liberated at all times,
one subject to relapse,
one not subject to relapse.
Subject to decline,
not subject to decline,
and capable of volition.
The worldling and the one who has reached the lineage stage are capable of guarding [the wholesome roots].
One who has desisted from fear, one who has desisted from fearlessness,
and one who is capable of progress.
Incapable of entering [the path],
destined,
undestined.
One who has entered the path,
one established in the fruit, and one who has reached the summit.
The noble one who abides for an eon,
and the ignoble one.
The Learner,
the One Beyond Training, and the One who is Neither Learner nor Beyond Training.
The Perfectly Enlightened One, possessing the threefold knowledge and the six direct knowledges.
A Pratyekabuddha,
one liberated both ways,
one liberated by wisdom.
The body-witness,
the one attained to vision,
and the one liberated by faith.
The follower by dhamma,
the follower by faith,
and the one who returns seven times at most.
One who goes from family to family,
a single-seed attainer,
and a once-returner.
Non-returner who attains parinirvāṇa in the intermediate state; non-returner who attains parinirvāṇa upon landing.
One who attains final nibbāna without exertion;
one who attains final nibbāna with exertion;
and one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm.
The stream-enterer,
one practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry,
and the once-returner.
One practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning;
a non-returner;
one practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning.
The Arahant;
one practicing for the realization of the fruit of Arahantship—
this is the single [type].
